title: Card
summary: A panel that groups content about one thing: the surface in an edge of the border color with the large radius, an optional header with a title and a description, a body and an optional footer of actions, its parts apart by a line.
use: Content about one thing, set apart from the page: a registration, a delivery address.
A short form or a summary with the actions that belong to it, in its footer.
notFor: A choice: that is the card variant of a checkbox or a radio group, a whole option drawn as a panel.
A link or an action as a whole panel: a card is not clickable, and its actions are buttons in its footer.
A window over the page: that is a modal.
A message about the page: that is a callout.

parts.root: The panel: the surface in its edge.
parts.header: The title and the description, over a line.
parts.title: The name of what the card holds, as a minor heading.
parts.description: A sentence under the title that says more.

variants.outline: The one look: the surface in an edge, as a window of the terminal frame is.

sizes.md: Every card: as wide as its column, as tall as its content.

states.rest: Always: a card is not interactive, so it has no other state. What is in it has its own.

rules: The title is a heading, at the level the page's outline puts the card at, so a card is a section of the page that a reader can jump to.
A card takes no focus and has no role of its own: what is in it, a link, a field or a button, takes the focus, in the order it is read.
Where a card is a landmark of the page, such as a summary that a reader needs to find, it is a `section` whose accessible name is its title, by `aria-labelledby`.

forcedColors: The card's edge is a real border, which forced colors keep, so the card stands apart from the page, which forced colors paint in the same color as the card.
The lines between its header, body and footer are borders too.
motion: Nothing moves: a card has no state to change into.
content: The title names what the card holds, in sentence case without a period: Registration, Delivery address.
The description is one sentence that says more: Harbour Conf 2027, Lisbon.
The footer holds the actions that belong to the card, each a button, the one it leads to last: Later, then Register.
notes: The kind is the one in use, Nuxt UI's outline. Its soft and subtle cards are on the raised color, without and with an edge, and its solid one inverts the panel into the text color, for which the system has no role: they are left out.

The edge is `color.border`, as the frame's window's is, not the field border of an overlay: a card frames content in the page, while an overlay lies over other content and is told apart from it by its edge, at 3:1.

The paddings are those from 64rem up. Below it, the system's compact width, every part's `padding-inline` and the body's `padding-block` are `space.16`, and the header's and the footer's `padding-block` `space.12`, as the frame's paddings narrow there too; a gallery's test runs at a desktop width, so the state table holds the wide card.

The line under the body is there only when a footer follows it, as its width with and without a footer says; its style and its color are the header's line's either way. A card without a header or a footer has only its body, the same distance from its edges.
A footer of actions lays them out at its end, `space.12` apart, as a modal's footer does. The footer is a box around them, so the spec checks its padding and not their place.

ui-vue.library: Nuxt UI 4.12, themed by ui-vue's app config
ui-vue.today: The outline variant is its default: the surface, the large radius, its parts apart by a line of `color.border`, the title a minor heading in mono and the description in the secondary text color. Its paddings are the spec's, 16 px and 20 px from 64rem, restated at Tailwind's `sm:` to cancel Nuxt UI's wider one. In forced colors its edge, a ring, is drawn as a border in `CanvasText`.

deviations.summary: The card's edge is a ring of `color.border`, a box shadow, and a border only in forced colors. So the rows for the root's `border-color`, `border-style` and `border-width` do not hold, nor its `box-shadow` of none.
Its title is a `div`, not a heading, so the card is not a section of the page's outline. A heading has to be passed in its `title` slot.

It draws its lines with `divide-y`, which colors only a part that is not the last, so a body without a footer keeps Tailwind's preflight `currentcolor` on the line it does not draw. So the row for the body's `border-block-end-color` does not hold there.
Its gallery marks no example with `data-spec`.

beyond: The soft and subtle variants, on the raised color without and with an edge, and the solid one, in the text color.
A card drawn as another element, by its `as` prop.
